values-and-names.title: From names to a computed value
values-and-names.summary: A data-dependency map for the lesson’s study-time calculation. Arrows mean “supplies a value to”; they do not mean that a name stores another name.

nodes.label: minutes_per_day = 25
nodes.description: This name refers to the integer 25.

nodes.label: days = 4
nodes.description: This name refers to the integer 4.
Multiplication evaluates the two input values and produces 100.

nodes.label: total = 100
nodes.description: Assignment binds total to the result; the two input bindings remain unchanged.

nodes.label: Total: 100 minutes
nodes.description: The f-string reads total and print writes the formatted text.

steps.title: Bind two input names
steps.explanation: The assignments establish two independent name-to-value bindings: 25 and 4.

steps.title: Evaluate the right side
steps.explanation: Reading both names supplies the integers to multiplication. Neither input is changed.

steps.title: Bind the result
steps.explanation: The product is 100. The assignment creates the total binding after evaluating the right side.

steps.title: Format the output
steps.explanation: The f-string produces Total: 100 minutes. Formatting does not turn the stored integer into a string.

functions.title: One function call, from arguments to return value
functions.summary: Follow print(study_minutes(3)). The default length supplies 25 for this call; return and print have separate jobs.

nodes.label: study_minutes(3)
nodes.description: The caller supplies one positional argument: sessions is 3.

nodes.label: sessions = 3; length = 25
nodes.description: Parameter bindings belong to this call. Omitting length selects its default.

nodes.label: return 75
nodes.description: The call finishes and yields the integer 75 to the caller.

nodes.label: print(75)
nodes.description: The caller prints 75. The output operation is outside study_minutes.

steps.title: Enter the call
steps.explanation: The definition already exists. Calling it creates this call’s parameter bindings; it does not run both example calls at once.

steps.title: Compute locally
steps.explanation: 3 × 25 evaluates to 75. The function has produced a value but has not displayed it.

steps.title: Return to the caller
steps.explanation: return ends this call and supplies 75 wherever study_minutes(3) was used.

steps.title: Use the returned value
steps.explanation: The outer print displays 75. The next example, study_minutes(2, length=15), is a separate call with result 30.
